items.title: Kering turnaround hopes hit by drop in Gucci sales
items.summary: Philippine business press carries the Kering Q3 results, noting Gucci sales fell 6% to EUR 1.29 billion (about half of group profit) and Kering shares dropped 11% on the news. Coverage flags management departures at sister brands Saint Laurent and Alexander McQueen as a sign of continued internal instability, and quotes Kering's finance chief pledging discipline while footfall, especially in China, keeps weighing on results.

items.title: "Gucci" yot khai ded -6% mae phayayam prap racha deung luk kha, reng pid 125 ran
items.summary: Thai business-media coverage of Kering's Q3 results takes a skeptical tone, headlining that Gucci's sales keep falling ('ลดแล้วก็ยังร่วง') despite price adjustments meant to lure shoppers back, and that the brand is accelerating store closures toward a 125-store target. Analysts are quoted saying turnaround progress is still at a very early stage, and the piece frames Gucci's problems as structural (China wealth pressures, soft global demand) rather than merely tactical.

items.title: How the third quarter shows luxury industry can't rely on walk-ins anymore
items.summary: Australian trade press analyzes Q3 2026 luxury earnings across Hermes, Kering, Prada and Zegna, noting Gucci (still ~39% of Kering revenue) fell 6% comparable with its own stores down 9%, driven by lower APAC traffic, particularly Mainland China and Japan. Kering's CEO is quoted saying traffic is the main constraint while conversion and ticket size held up. The piece frames this as evidence the sector can no longer count on walk-in footfall and must lean harder on direct client relationships.

items.title: Gucci hung bua riu du luan vi ban sneaker 1.000 USD 'Made in China'
items.summary: Vietnamese business media reports Gucci's new Demna-designed Drip sneaker (~USD 1,000) is labeled 'Made in China,' the first time in over a century a flagship Gucci shoe has carried that label, and frames it as drawing public criticism ('hung bua riu du luan'). The article links this to Gucci's steep revenue slide (EUR 10.49bn in 2022 to EUR 7.7bn in 2024) and quotes a Milan consultant calling 'Made in China' bad for the brand's image, questioning why shoppers should keep paying luxury prices for non-European-made goods. Included despite a late-Sept publish date because it is the clearest SEA-language record of ongoing public reaction to a still-live controversy; no fresher vernacular write-up was found.

items.title: Thai fans celebrate Billkin and PP Krit as 'the Gucci BA couple from Thailand' at Milan show
items.summary: Thai fan account post reacting to Gucci's The Store Show in Milan, tagging both Thai ambassadors Billkin and PP Krit with hashtags #GUCCISS27xPPKRIT and #GUCCISS27xBILLKIN. Pure fandom enthusiasm around ambassador appearances rather than independent brand judgment; representative of continuing high-volume Thai fan engagement with Gucci's ambassador roster into late October as the hashtags kept recirculating.

items.title: Thai actors top fashion week global metric charts
items.summary: Bangkok Post reports Thai actors, including Gucci ambassadors Billkin and PP Krit, ranked among the highest-performing celebrities by global fashion-week media-impact metrics during the recent Milan shows. Framed as a national pride/soft-power story about Thai star power rather than an evaluative verdict on Gucci's product; counted as activation-adjacent fan coverage.

items.title: Threads post labels Gucci one of the 'most overrated' luxury brands
items.summary: A Threads post ranking 'most overrated luxury brands' names Gucci first, criticizing 'screaming logos,' 'poor leather quality' and 'mass-market hype,' contrasting it with brands seen as more exclusive. Organic negative consumer opinion (not brand-staged), fitting the design-criticism/quality-complaint negative category under the sentiment rubric; included under the mandatory critical-angle search requirement.

items.title: Kering lao doc khi doanh thu Gucci giam 6% trong quy III
items.summary: Vietnamese-language financial wire coverage of Kering's Q3 2026 results reports Gucci's 6% comparable sales decline and Kering's stock slide, aimed at a Vietnamese investor/business readership. Mirrors the T1 wire figures but signals the story's penetration into SEA local-language financial media beyond English-language trade press.

items.title: Kering Quy 2/2026: Gucci co dau hieu khoi sac nho cac mau tui xach moi
items.summary: Vietnamese fashion-business outlet revisits Kering's quarterly trajectory, noting Gucci showed tentative signs of stabilizing earlier in 2026 on the strength of new handbag styles before the Q3 slump reported this week. Provides SEA-language context connecting the two in Vietnamese entertainment/fashion press, with a cautiously mixed tone (neither fully negative nor positive) on the turnaround's durability.

items.title: "PP Krit Shines as Gucci Ambassador at Milan Fashion Week" trends on X
items.summary: X's trending-topics module surfaced continued Thai fan chatter around PP Krit's Gucci ambassador role tied to Milan Fashion Week coverage recirculating in late October. Fandom-driven volume rather than independent product judgment; damped to mild magnitude per the fandom-trap guidance in the sentiment rubric.

items.source: Weibo - FAQ/explainer account (Chinese-language, SEA price-gap angle)
items.title: Explainer thread on shrinking Gucci China/overseas price gap after 2026 cuts
items.summary: A Weibo explainer/FAQ-style post discusses how Gucci's 2026 domestic China price cuts (up to 40%) narrowed the China-vs-overseas price gap to under 10%, a topic relevant to SEA duty-free/travel-retail shoppers (Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam) who previously bought Gucci bags while traveling in China for arbitrage. Comment-style community content discussing practical buying strategy rather than brand sentiment per se; signals eroding of a prior cross-border value proposition.

items.title: PurseForum members discuss Demna's new Gucci bag drops
items.summary: Long-running handbag-collector community thread discussing Demna's newest Gucci bag releases, with mixed member reactions ranging from curiosity about the redesigned icons to skepticism about pricing versus perceived design novelty. Genuine enthusiast community opinion (not brand press), used here for the community channel; sentiment is mixed rather than uniformly positive.
